title: Weighted MaxSAT by unsat cores (OLL, split weights)
description: Weighted MaxSAT with the core-guided algorithm OLL. A soft clause of weight W becomes W unit soft constraints (its copies, drop(C,I) for I = 1..W), the simplest form of the weight splitting of WPM1 and weighted OLL: every core raises the lower bound by one unit, a core is relaxed copy by copy, and its totaliser counts violated copies. The first satisfiable call is optimal. Instances of the weighted MaxHS example (maxsat-ihs): compare the number of cores with the hitting-set loop, which takes the weights directly.

fragments.name: shared
fragments.text:
% The instance (Instances tab): soft(C,W) is a soft clause C with weight W, hard(C) a hard
% clause; pos(C,V) and neg(C,V) are the literals of clause C.
cl(C) :- soft(C,_).
cl(C) :- hard(C).
var(V) :- pos(_,V).
var(V) :- neg(_,V).
% Weight splitting: the I-th unit of the weight of soft clause C.
copy(C,I) :- soft(C,W), I = 1..W.

fragments.name: abstraction
fragments.text:
% Only a source of the starting assumptions: its optimal model drops nothing, so G(M) assumes
% every unit copy of every soft clause kept. All the work happens in the solver C.
{ drop(C,I) : copy(C,I) }.
#minimize { 1,C,I : drop(C,I) }.
#show drop/2.

fragments.name: check
fragments.text:
% An assignment that satisfies the hard clauses and every soft clause that is not dropped.
{ t(V) } :- var(V).
sat(C) :- pos(C,V), t(V).
sat(C) :- neg(C,V), not t(V).
:- hard(C), not sat(C).
:- copy(C,I), not drop(C,I), not sat(C).
unsat(C) :- soft(C,_), not sat(C).
#show t/1.
#show unsat/1.
% The cost of a solution: its violated soft clauses (every model the last call can return
% has the same number, the lower bound).
#minimize { W,C : unsat(C), soft(C,W) }.
% viol(T): the soft constraint T is violated. The soft constraints are the soft clauses
% (T = drop(C,I), a unit copy) and the totaliser outputs added by relax (T = over(K,J)).
viol(drop(C,I)) :- drop(C,I).

#program relax(k).
% core(k,T): the k-th unsat core, one fact per soft constraint in it. At least one of them is
% violated in every solution: that is the +1 of the lower bound. over(k,J) says that at least
% J of them are violated; each over(k,J) for J >= 2 becomes a new soft constraint (assumed
% false by the loop), so a solution pays for every violation beyond the first.
size(k,N) :- N = #count { T : core(k,T) }.
over(k,J) :- size(k,N), J = 2..N, #count { T : core(k,T), viol(T) } >= J.
viol(over(k,J)) :- over(k,J).

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

# Core-guided MaxSAT (OLL, Morgado, Dodaro and Marques-Silva): one solver, called under
# assumptions "every soft constraint holds". Each unsat core raises the lower bound by one;
# its soft constraints are relaxed (no longer assumed) and replaced by the totaliser outputs
# over(k,J) of relax(k), assumed false. The first satisfiable call is optimal.
E = G(A.solve(optimal))            # every soft clause assumed kept
lower = 0
loop:
    track lower = lower
    X = C.solve(assume E)
    if X:
        log "optimum:", lower, "violated:", X.count(unsat/1)
        accept X
        stop
    K = C.core
    if K.size == 0: stop "the hard clauses are unsatisfiable"
    lower = lower + 1
    for a in K:                    # relax the core's soft constraints
        E = E.without(a)
    C.expand(relax, core = K)      # facts core(k,T): the core's atoms (B2)
    j = 2
    while j <= K.size:             # the new soft constraints: not over(k,j)
        o = C.atom("over", C.step, j)
        for a in o:
            E.push(a)
            E = E.flip(a)
        j = j + 1
